items.quote:
local loot = source and Dungeons.LootRows(source, instance, known or {}) or {}
	for _, entry in ipairs(known or {}) do
items.what: BossRows guards `known or {}` twice although its contract makes known non-optional: types/Namespace.lua:1774 declares `known: AGFDungeonBoss[]`, and the only caller, UI/WindowDungeons.lua:533, already passes `known or {}`.

items.quote: local instance = type(entry) == "table" and entry.InstanceID
items.what: Re-validation of AtlasLoot entries twelve lines after the same checks filtered them; read entry.InstanceID directly and drop the repeated `type(entry.items) == "table"` on the next line.

The trust-boundary check is the first one; lines 376-377 repeat it on already-validated values.

The entry.items recheck therefore occurs after possible external mutation, covered by the trust-boundary exclusion, so the proposed combined removal is not proven redundant.

items.quote:
local instance = type(entry) == "table" and entry.InstanceID
		if instance and (ns.Data.instances[instance] or ns.RaidByMap[instance]) and type(entry.items) == "table" then
items.what: The curated loop re-validates each page entry (type(entry) == "table", entry.InstanceID, type(entry.items) == "table") that the pages filter at Integrations/Dungeons.lua:360 already guaranteed when it built the list.
items.why: pages holds only entries that passed the same three checks 12 lines above, and nothing mutates them in between, so the repeated checks cannot fail; they hide the two checks on this line that do matter (the instance is known to ns.Data.instances or ns.RaidByMap). Reduce to `local instance = entry.InstanceID` and `if ns.Data.instances[instance] or ns.RaidByMap[instance] then`.
items.reason: The page entries retain references to AtlasLoot-owned tables rather than validated copies, and Source calls its yielding callback while processing earlier pages. These checks re-read third-party addon data across suspension, covered by the trust-boundary exclusion.

items.quote: function Dungeons.Source(yield)
items.what: Integrations/Dungeons.lua (647 lines) mixes: the headless catalogue and page model (ForCharacter, List, Quest, Chain, Page, ChainPosition, lines 11-285 and 595-619); client and addon readers (Journal, the Encounter Journal, 309-337; Source, the AtlasLoot adapter, 339-420, 78 lines nested seven deep); row presentation (LootRows, 479-547, with item info and locale text); guidance actions (Go, GoEntrance, 287-307, 549-576); and saved preferences (Planned, SetPlanned, 621-647).

items.quote: local prefs, key = ns.Prefs(), "dungeon:" .. instance
items.what: The dungeon journey key format "dungeon:" .. id is rebuilt by concatenation in every consumer instead of one function owned by the planner that produces it.

The inspected planner and UI consumers, including origin/cb/route-stop-api, construct identifiers rather than branch on an untyped closed enum; centralizing construction is outside this lens.

items.quote: function Integrations.TravelLine(step)
items.what: Both callers of TravelLine repeat the same choice between it and Travel: UI/Overview.lua:59 and UI/WindowGuide.lua:146 each write `index == 1 and ns.Integrations.Travel(step) or ns.Integrations.TravelLine(step)`.
items.why: The rule (step 1 shows the line fetched after the rebuild, a later row asks Shortest Path once on hover) belongs to the travel module, which already knows which step it fetched for (travel.key), yet each caller carries it. The repeated and/or also falls through: when step 1 has no cached line (the player stands in its area, where RefreshTravel deliberately fetches none), the hover calls TravelLine and asks Shortest Path anyway. One function answering 'the travel line for this row' would hold both the rule and that case.
items.reason: UI/Overview.lua:59 and UI/WindowGuide.lua:146 both write `index == 1 and ns.Integrations.Travel(step) or ns.Integrations.TravelLine(step)`, and a cached nil line for a here step falls through to a fetch on hover. Give Integrations one row-facing function for this choice, keeping the cached-only callers (Tracker, Pins) as they are?

items.quote: local function Copy(value)
items.what: Copy (Integrations/Providers.lua:9-18) is a hand-rolled recursive table copy; the client's CopyTable (Blizzard_SharedXML TableUtil.lua) does the same and can replace it.
items.why: CopyTable is in the pinned Ketho annotations (.types/vscode-wow-api/Annotations/Core/FrameXML/Blizzard_SharedXML/TableUtil.lua), so it is part of the mainline UI the Forever client runs; it must be confirmed on the Forever client itself, which this review could not do. rg 'CopyTable' over the repository returns nothing, so the fix also needs the global in .luacheckrc and a stub in tests/harness.lua. Behaviour to preserve: Copy returns a non-table unchanged, so Copy(summary) with a nil summary (line 99) needs a guard, since CopyTable(nil) errors. The shallow-copy loops at UI/PvP.lua:139-143 and UI/Sound.lua:64-67 are the same wheel (CopyTable(t, true)).

items.quote: if type(api) ~= "table" or type(api.version) ~= "number" or api.version < 1 then
items.what: Three companion probes return the same ready/missing/outdated answer from the same steps (API table, numeric version of at least 1, a list of required functions): Legacy() (Integrations/Providers.lua:25-39), SkillUp() (Integrations/SkillUp.lua:11-28) and the inline one in Providers.DungeonEntrance (Integrations/Providers.lua:137-148). No copy is canonical; SkillUp() is the most complete.
items.why: Drift already present: SkillUp() reports "outdated" when the addon is loaded but its global or API is absent (C_AddOns.IsAddOnLoaded), Legacy() and DungeonEntrance report "missing" whenever the global is nil; Legacy() builds its required-call list inline per call, SkillUp keeps SKILLUP_CALLS. The three states feed sibling UI branches (UI/WindowCompletion.lua:77-79, UI/WindowProfessions.lua:96-98, UI/Overview.lua:373-374), so a rule change for what counts as outdated needs all three. SPF() in Integrations/Integrations.lua is deliberately different (version equality, list held by tests/contract_spec.lua) and is not part of this.
items.reason: Legacy validates four Legacy callbacks, SkillUp validates three unrelated profession callbacks and loaded-without-global state, and DungeonEntrance validates one Tweaks callback then its returned point. These independent addon contracts can change independently, and the shared version/function checks are small guard idioms excluded by the lens.

items.quote: local api = TweaksForever and TweaksForever.API
items.what: Providers.DungeonEntrance (Integrations/Providers.lua:136-147) restates the Tweaks Forever API version gate that Tweaks() in Integrations/Integrations.lua:141-148 owns; expose that one accessor (with the missing/outdated reason) and use it here.
items.why: rg 'api\.version|\.API\b' shows the same test, type(api) ~= "table" or type(api.version) ~= "number" or api.version < 1, at Integrations/Integrations.lua:143 and Integrations/Providers.lua:141-143. Integrations.lua carries the rule's reason ("A range, not an equality, so a newer additive Tweaks Forever never silently disables..."); a change to the supported version range has to be made in both files or the trainer hint and the dungeon entrance disagree about whether Tweaks Forever is usable. The copies differ only in that Providers also reports "missing"/"outdated" and checks the DungeonEntrance member. Legacy() (Providers.lua:25-39) and SkillUp() (Integrations.lua:224-241) are the same ready/missing/outdated validator shape for other addons, each with its own required-call list; those are per-addon contracts and are not raised.
items.reason: The shared API table/version predicate is a small guard covered by the parallel-implementations lens's explicit exclusion. The surrounding contracts differ: Tweaks supports training consumers with member-specific checks, while DungeonEntrance validates its own member and reports missing, outdated and unknown states.

items.quote: local values = lib.Item.GetAll(id, { "npcDrops", "objectDrops", "itemDrops" })
items.what: The QuestieDB item field list read here restates the list Fit validates in Integrations/QuestieSource.lua:43 (ENTITIES Item fields), as does the { "spawns" } read at QuestieObjectives.lua:82 against GIVER_FIELDS (QuestieSource.lua:38); export the field lists from QuestieSource (the canonical home, where the contract is checked) and read through them.

items.quote: need[16], kinds[16] = 1, "event"
items.what: The planner's need-slot layout is written as bare numbers here: 16 for the explore slot (lines 161-162), `slot > 3` for the kill and use range (115, 136), `index + 3` and `index > 4` for the item range (151, 154). items.quote: if x and y and x >= 0 and x <= 100 and y >= 0 and y <= 100 then
items.what: QuestieDB's spawns table (area to a list of 0-100 x,y pairs) is parsed and range-checked twice: Places in Integrations/QuestieObjectives.lua:27-41 and Giver in Integrations/QuestieSource.lua:277-284 (canonical: QuestieSource.lua, which owns the QuestieDB format and already passes its Map resolver in as mapOf).
items.why: Same walk (pairs over areas, resolve the map, tonumber both coordinates, reject outside 0-100, divide by 100). Differences: Giver rounds to four places, Places keeps the raw fraction and buckets it; ReadDungeonSource (:503-507) reads the same shape for entrances with no range check, relying on Model.ValidPlace. A change in how a spawn pair is validated or scaled must be made in each. The bucketing after the parse is a real difference; the parse and validation are not.
items.reason: Giver checks numeric area keys, caches named giver records and rounds points to four decimals; Places requires yard geometry, retains precision for cell reach, yields per map and selects ranked clusters, while entrances use converted support points and ValidPlace. The overlapping tonumber/range/divide fragment is a small validation idiom rather than a duplicate of those distinct algorithms.

items.quote: function ns.ReadDungeonSource(yield)
items.what: Two responsibilities in one 604-line file: the quest catalogue (contract fit, geometry helpers, Build, the login coroutine and status, lines 1-462) and the dungeon tab's source reader ns.ReadDungeonSource (lines 464-604, one 137-line function: entrances, NPC-to-instance, item loot and rewards, objective text).

They share only Fit, MissingField and ENTITIES. Split: the reader moves to its own file beside QuestieObjectives.lua, with the fit check exported the way ns.QuestieFields already is; the duplicated instance map (see the parallel-implementations finding) is the place the two halves have already drifted.
items.reason: Move ns.ReadDungeonSource (Integrations/QuestieSource.lua:464-604, one 137-line function for entrances, NPCs and loot, read on demand by the dungeon tab) into its own file beside the login-time quest catalogue? Fit and MissingField are the helpers both would share.

items.quote: instanceOf[area] = instance
items.what: The area-to-instance map is built twice in one file: Build (Integrations/QuestieSource.lua:260-263, read at :345) and ns.ReadDungeonSource (:492-501, read at :522-523). Neither is shared; the ReadDungeonSource copy is the fuller one.
items.why: Both answer which instance an area or its parent zone belongs to. Differences: ReadDungeonSource also maps ZoneDB's alias areas (dungeon[2]) and skips raids and instances the data lacks; Build maps only zones.instances and filters by bundled.instances afterwards. The raid filter is intentional (the dungeon tab), the missing aliases in Build look like drift: an NPC in an alias area counts as inside the dungeon while a quest whose zoneOrSort is that alias area gets no quest.dungeon unless the parent lookup rescues it. The parent lookup itself is also written twice (Parent() at :250-252 and inline at :522).
items.reason: Integrations/QuestieSource.lua builds the area-to-instance map twice and the copies disagree: Build (260-263, read at 345) lacks the ZoneDB dungeon alias areas that ns.ReadDungeonSource (492-501) includes. Input: a quest whose zoneOrSort is a dungeon alias area (headless probe: 999906). Wrong result: quest.dungeon is nil, so the quest is not filed under its dungeon, while the dungeon source lists the same area's NPCs under instance 43.

items.quote:
if ns.Invalidate then
		ns.Invalidate()
	end
items.what: Settled guards ns.Invalidate's existence, but Core/Core.lua:808 defines it at file scope and the TOC loads Core\Core.lua before Integrations\QuestieSource.lua; types/Namespace.lua:647 declares it non-optional, and this file's own Questie callback (line 444) calls it unguarded.

If it ever fired, the route held for the catalogue build would stay held with no error. Call ns.Invalidate() directly, or drop Settled for ns.Invalidate().

items.quote: local LINK = 100 -- yards: a giver this near a bundled town's place stands in that town (tools/gen_quests.py LINK)
items.what: The town-linkage distance is restated by hand in three runtime files, each citing tools/gen_quests.py LINK (gen_quests.py:400, the canonical home): QuestieSource.lua:15, Integrations/Integrations.lua:495 (LINK) and Planning/Model.lua:1186 (AGREE); the generator should emit it into Data/Geometry.lua (or one ns constant) and the three read it.
items.why: rg '\bLINK\b' over *.lua and *.py: definitions at tools/gen_quests.py:400, QuestieSource.lua:15, Integrations.lua:495; Model.lua:1186 names it AGREE with the same citation. Data/Geometry.lua carries the value only in a header comment (line 13, 'single linkage at 100 yd'), no field. QuestieSource's copy must equal the generator's: Hub() re-implements nearest_hub's LINK-yard cell grid over the townAnchors the generator linked at LINK, so a changed generator value silently mis-assigns hubs. The Integrations and Model copies are tolerances defined as 'the town linkage' by their own comments, so they are meant to follow it too.
items.reason: Applied on cb/sift-decisions.

items.quote: local private = zoneDB and zoneDB["private"]
items.what: `zoneDB and` cannot be false when Support.Get returns nil: the previous line ends in `or {}`; either drop the `and` or drop the `or {}`, one guard is enough.
